1.title: Azure Files and Blob Storage
1.text: Welcome to Module six: Azure Files and Blob Storage. It covers the exam area Implement and manage storage. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. Create and configure a file share in Azure Storage. Create and configure a container in Blob Storage. Configure storage tiers. Configure snapshots and soft delete for Azure Files. Configure blob lifecycle management. Configure blob versioning. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Implement and manage storage (fifteen-twenty percent). Exam format: one hundred minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official Microsoft Learn A Z-one hundred four study guide, skills measured as of October twenty-six, two thousand twenty-three.

1.title: Azure Files
1.text: Azure Files. Azure Files gives fully managed file shares in the cloud, reachable over S M B (Server Message Block) (and N F S (Network File System) on Premium) and mountable from Windows, Linux and mac O S. Create. Create a file share in a storage account, set a quota and a tier. Mount. Use the mount script from the portal (S M B uses port four hundred forty-five, which some networks block). Tiers. Transaction optimized, Hot, Cool (standard accounts); Premium (S S D). Snapshots. Share snapshots are point-in-time, read-only copies; incremental (only changes use space). Soft delete. Keeps a deleted share for a retention period (one to three sixty-five days) so it can be undeleted.

1.title: Azure Files, continued
1.text: Azure Files. The figure shows this: Azure Files: shares, snapshots and soft delete. Exam tip: "Recover a share that was deleted by mistake" equals soft delete for Azure Files. "Recover an older version of files in a share" equals share snapshots.

1.title: Blob Storage
1.text: Blob Storage. Blob Storage holds unstructured objects in containers. Block blob. Documents, images, media (most common). Append blob. Logs (append only). Page blob. Random access, V M disks.

1.title: Blob Storage, continued
1.text: Blob Storage. Public access level. Private (default), Blob (anonymous read of blobs), Container (anonymous list and read). Access control. R B A C, S A S, stored access policy, access keys.

1.title: Access tiers
1.text: Access tiers. The figure shows this: Blob access tiers: hot, cool, cold and archive.

1.title: Access tiers, continued
1.text: Access tiers. Hot. For: Frequently accessed data. Storage cost: Highest. Access cost: Lowest. Cool. For: Infrequent, kept at least thirty days. Storage cost: Lower. Access cost: Higher. Cold. For: Rare, kept at least ninety days. Storage cost: Lower still. Access cost: Higher. Archive. For: Rarely accessed, kept at least one hundred eighty days, offline. Storage cost: Lowest. Access cost: Highest, must be rehydrated (hours) before reading. Minimum retention periods apply (early deletion charges). Exam tip: Archive blobs cannot be read until rehydrated to hot or cool.

1.title: Lifecycle management, versioning and soft delete
1.text: Lifecycle management, versioning and soft delete. Lifecycle management. Rules that move blobs to cooler tiers or delete them based on age (since modification or creation) or last access. Versioning. Automatically keeps previous versions when a blob is overwritten or deleted; you can restore an older version. Soft delete (blobs, containers). Retains deleted blobs or containers for a set period for recovery. Snapshots (blobs). Manual point-in-time read-only copy. Exam tip: "Move blobs to cool after thirty days and delete after one year" equals a lifecycle management rule.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Users need a shared network drive in Azure that Windows and Linux machines can mount. Which service fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Azure Files. Azure Files provides S M B and N F S file shares.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A file share was deleted by mistake. What should have been enabled? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Soft delete for Azure Files. Soft delete retains deleted shares for recovery.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Data is rarely accessed and can wait hours to be read. Which tier is cheapest to store? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Archive. Archive has the lowest storage cost and requires rehydration.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Blobs should move to the cool tier after thirty days automatically. What should be configured? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A lifecycle management rule. Lifecycle rules transition blobs based on age.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A blob is overwritten and the old content must be recoverable. What should be enabled? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Blob versioning. Versioning keeps previous versions of blobs.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A container allows anonymous read access to individual blobs but not listing. Which public access level is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Blob. The Blob level allows anonymous reads of blobs but not listing the container.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which protocols does Azure Files support? Answer: S M B (and N F S on Premium). Question two. What is a share snapshot? Answer: A point-in-time, read-only copy of a file share. Question three. Name the four blob tiers. Answer: Hot, cool, cold and archive.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What must happen before an archive blob can be read? Answer: It must be rehydrated to hot or cool. Question five. What does lifecycle management do? Answer: Moves blobs to other tiers or deletes them by rules. Question six. Which blob type suits logs? Answer: Append blob.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Azure Files: S M B or N F S shares, snapshots, soft delete, tiers. Blob types: block, append, page; container public access private or blob or container. Tiers: hot, cool (thirty d), cold (ninety d), archive (one hundred eighty d, offline). Management: lifecycle rules, versioning, soft delete, snapshots.
